qs.q: A patient is evaluated for glycemic status and found to have a fasting plasma glucose level of 115 mg/dL (6.4 mmol/L). How should this finding be categorized?
o: Impaired fasting glucose diagnostic of prediabetes
Normal upper limit of fasting blood glucose level
Impaired glucose tolerance based on oral load
Provisional diagnosis of established type diabetes
qs.e: Prediabetes is defined by impaired fasting glucose when fasting glucose is between 100 and 125 mg/dL. A fasting concentration of 99 mg/dL or lower represents the upper limit of normal.

qs.q: A 55-year-old man presents with episodic diaphoresis, tremulousness, and confusion that consistently resolve after drinking orange juice. Laboratory evaluation reveals a fasting plasma glucose level of 42 mg/dL. Which constellation of findings confirms this diagnosis?
o: Postprandial glucose of 140 mg/dL, elevated C-peptide, and lack of symptom relief with feeding
Fasting glucose above 126 mg/dL, metabolic acidosis, and positive urinary acetoacetate
Symptoms during fasting, concurrent glucose below 50 mg/dL, and resolution after carbohydrate intake
Serum osmolarity over 320 mOsm/L, normal pH, and severe dehydration without ketosis
qs.e: Whipple's triad requires hypoglycemic symptoms, low plasma glucose during symptoms, and relief when glucose is restored. The other sets describe diabetic ketoacidosis, hyperosmolar states, or non-hypoglycemic conditions.

qs.q: A 38-year-old healthcare worker presents with recurrent symptomatic hypoglycemia, a low fasting plasma glucose level, and markedly elevated serum insulin. What is the primary diagnostic utility of measuring serum C-peptide in this patient?
o: Differentiating autoimmune insulin antibodies from insulin receptor gene mutations
Assessing acute hepatic glycogen breakdown secondary to excessive glucagon secretion
Evaluating total functional beta-cell reserve prior to initiating sulfonylurea therapy
Distinguishing endogenous hyperinsulinism from exogenous insulin administration
qs.e: C-peptide is co-secreted with endogenous insulin in equimolar amounts, so a low C-peptide with high insulin indicates exogenous administration, whereas elevated C-peptide indicates endogenous hyperinsulinism. Evaluating beta-cell reserve is used in managing established diabetes rather than diagnosing acute hypoglycemia.

qs.q: Diagnostic criterion for diabetes mellitus using fasting plasma glucose is ---
o: B. ≥ 7.8 mmol/L
A. ≥ 6.1 mmol/L
D. ≥ 6.5 mmol/L
C. ≥ 7.0 mmol/L
qs.e: A fasting plasma glucose of 7.0 mmol/L or higher meets the diagnostic threshold for diabetes.

qs.q: The diagnostic criterion for diabetes mellitus using fasting plasma glucose is
o: ≥6.1 mmol/L (110 mg/dL)
≥11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) on any sample
≥8.0 mmol/L (144 mg/dL)
≥7.0 mmol/L (126 mg/dL)
qs.e: WHO/ADA: FPG ≥7.0 mmol/L on two occasions = diabetes (option D is also valid on a symptomatic random sample).
